intent: Refactor to resolve 13 SonarQube findings with behaviour and log output unchanged: decompose runProviderBackups, displayStartupConfig, checkProvider, Run, checkProvidersDefined and TestGiteaOrgsRepositoryBackup into helpers; extract backup status titles into constants + backupStatusTitle; remove duplicate TestPublicGitLabRepositoryBackup2; Dockerfile: merge RUN instructions, sort apk packages, quote ${TAG}.
residual_risks: internal/backup.go:475 (maintainability, P2, confidence 100, demoted from #1): createWorkingDir repeats the GIT_WORKING_DIR / backupDir+workingDIRName default already implemented by resolveWorkingDir (internal/backup.go:140-146). If the default changes in one, startup would create a different directory than runProviderBackups cleans up via cleanupWorkingDir. The logic was already inline in Run at c77f548 and the diff only moved it. Suggested: in createWorkingDir, use `workingDIR := resolveWorkingDir(backupDIR)`.

checkProvidersDefined now computes bitbucketAPITokenComplete before the provider map loop (internal/backup.go) instead of inside it. The old code depended on Go map iteration order and could double-count BitBucket when OAuth was visited first; the new order is deterministic. Only the count==0 check consumes the count, so observable behaviour is unchanged, but it departs slightly from the 'behaviour unchanged' claim and BitBucket matching now uses EqualFold instead of ToLower== (equivalent for ASCII env values).

collectProviderBackupResults replaces five if-blocks with a table of {env var, run func}; it is 0% covered offline, so a mis-paired entry (for example Gitea mapped to the GitHub runner) would only surface in live-provider tests, which skip without credentials. Reviewers verified the pairing by reading the diff against c77f548.

The claim that log output is unchanged for displayStartupConfig and the extracted logProvider* helpers rests on line-by-line comparison against c77f548; no test asserts the log text. Messages and order were found identical, including the 'Gitlab backup LFS' casing and the 'Organistations' typo, which are deliberately preserved through the shared helpers' label parameters.
testing_gaps: internal/notify.go:31 (testing, P2, confidence 75, demoted from #3): the new backupStatusTitle has no test. Slack, ntfy and Telegram notifications all take their title from it, and nothing asserts the (succeeded, failed) -> title mapping, so swapped branches or corrupted emoji constants (two carry an invisible U+FE0F prefix) would ship wrong titles with the suite green. Suggested: table-driven TestBackupStatusTitle covering (1,0)->titleBackupsSucceeded, (1,1)->titleBackupsErrors, (0,1)->titleBackupsFailed, (0,0)->titleBackupsFailed, asserting against literal strings rather than the constants.

internal/backup.go:369 (testing, P2, confidence 75, demoted from #2): the error branches of the extracted checkJustTokenProvider (66.7% covered) and checkUserAndPasswordProvider (57.1%) are not run offline. These produce the 'parameter X is not defined' messages for blank tokens or partial Azure DevOps / BitBucket credentials; the only existing test, TestCheckProvidersFailureWhenNoneDefined (internal/backup_test.go:787), covers the no-providers path. Suggested: table-driven tests for checkProvider and checkProvidersDefined using t.Setenv (blank GITHUB_TOKEN errors; Azure DevOps with only the user name errors naming the missing PAT with count 0; full Azure DevOps yields (1, nil); full BitBucket API-token plus OAuth counts as one provider).

validateStartupConfig error paths (GITHUB_ORGS without a token, nonexistent dir, stat failure) are not individually tested; only the undefined backup-dir case is reached, via TestFailureIfGitBackupDirUndefined.

createWorkingDir, scheduleBackups and runScheduledJob (interval and cron branches, the 'failed to create job' error) are 0% covered offline; the interval/cron branches block on waitForShutdown and are hard to test without injecting a signal.
